page.audience: People working with research, websites, code, files and apps on a computer
page.offer: Keep the task, tools, files and named coworkers together in one desktop workspace

sections.heading: AI coworkers. On your computer.
body: Phoenix is a desktop app that helps you research, build websites, write code, and work with files and apps.
evidence: README.md:7-32; actual product captures in assets/provenance.json
sections.user_question: What is Phoenix and why would I use it?
sections.purpose: Explain the literal product category and practical work before showing it.
sections.composition: 1280px contained, 60/40 split type and explanation, 100px maximum sans headline; a full-width real product screenshot follows. No scenic hero or invented dashboard chrome.
sections.compact: Stack title and explanation; preserve both in reading order. Keep task facts and the first CTA before the actual interface image.
sections.motion: First viewport is visible immediately. Hover motion is 1px; reduced motion disables it. No animated entrance hiding the main explanation.

sections.heading: Not just an answer. A place to do the work.
body: Start from a task, not a list of tools. Phoenix brings the conversation, files, browser and coworkers together.
sections.user_question: What could I actually ask it to do?
sections.purpose: Four practical examples, what each produces, and relevant coworkers. Explicitly not a running model.
sections.composition: 40/60 task index and one changing brief panel, separated by 64px. A task list, not three generic feature cards.
sections.compact: Two-column task picker above the single brief panel; native keyboard tab/arrow behavior remains.
sections.motion: Selection updates content directly, with stable panel height; optional one-time heading entrance only when initially below the viewport.

sections.heading: Meet your other coworkers.
body: Talk to Phoenix to coordinate a task, or go straight to the coworker you need. Their roles make the work easier to follow.
sections.purpose: Explain persistent role identities without anthropomorphic capability promises or a fake customer roster.
sections.composition: Narrow introduction beside a ruled two-column directory; selected coworker has an explicit description; other six roles are behind a native disclosure.
sections.compact: Introduction, directory, description and disclosure stack. Every role remains readable.
sections.motion: Small selected monogram tilt only; all content remains usable without motion.

sections.heading: Your computer. Your call.
body: Phoenix gives AI tools access to real work. That makes clear boundaries just as important as capability.
sections.user_question: What access does it have and where does my data go?
sections.purpose: Explain workspaces, provider choice and visible activity. Clearly disclose local-first is not offline AI.
sections.composition: Product control explanation beside a real settings capture. Definitions are readable rows, not decorative stats.
sections.compact: Explanation precedes the screenshot and explicit data-flow note; no hidden warning in a tooltip.
sections.motion: Static real image; minor one-time heading entrance with reduced-motion fallback.

sections.heading: A few straight answers.
body: Phoenix is in development, with Linux as its current target. This page is a product preview.
evidence: README.md:43,74-76; no public-release/signup endpoint configured for this page
sections.user_question: Can I use it yet, and what should I expect?
sections.purpose: Direct answers about release, supported provider routes, permissions and reliability limitations. No invented download, price, date or waitlist.
sections.composition: Editorial left title plus five native details rows, each answering one question.
sections.compact: Single-column native disclosures, comfortable touch targets and visible focus.
sections.motion: No animated content hiding; native disclosure behavior.
